newsitem.title: USA: Fed adds via overnight systems, no policy impact.
newsitem.headline: Fed adds via overnight systems, no policy impact.

text.p: The Federal Reserve injected reserves into the banking system via overnight system repurchase agreements on Tuesday, a Fed spokeswoman confirmed.
The Fed's open market operation had no monetary policy implications, market sources added.
The Federal Open Market Committee meeting is currently underway, with any announcement on interest rates expected at around 1415 EDT/1815 GMT.
The Fed could kick off the new two-week maintenance period with a five-day fixed system repurchase agreement on Thursday and reassess its position after the long Memorial Day weekend, they said.
Analysts still said a permanent injection of reserves via an outright purchase of bills was possible as early as this week. However, most do not see a bill pass until early next month.
The federal funds rate was trading at 5-5/8 percent, above its 5-1/2 percent target, at the time the Fed entered the market.
